history.dynasty: Kullu royal house (Raja Jagat Singh, per some sources); Pandava legend
history.period: CONFLICT (verify): 1652 CE / 16th century per some sources; Pandava-era origin per legend
history.summary: Hilltop Shiva temple at ~2,460 m in the Kath-Kuni (Pahari) style, with a 60-ft deodar-wood staff in front. Legend says Shiva killed the asura Jalandhara (variant: Kulanta the serpent, which took giant-serpent form to submerge life under water) with his trident and saved the Kullu valley from submersion. The staff is said to attract lightning ("bijli"), which shatters the shivalinga - popular claims of 12-year cycles are UNVERIFIED - and the priest reassembles it with butter and sattoo (gram-flour paste). Founding date CONFLICTS: 1652 CE / 16th century by Raja Jagat Singh per some sources vs Pandava-era legend. NOTE: eindiatourism.in's page on this temple wrongly pastes the Raghunath/Ayodhya-idol story onto it - do not trust that source. The site offers panoramic views of the Kullu and Parvati valleys; the Basheshwar Mahadev temple at Bajaura lies ~23 km away. CSV town 'Kullu' is approximate - the temple stands on a hilltop near Chansari village, reached by a ~3 km trek.

name: Bijli Mahadev Temple
town: Chansari (hilltop near Kullu town; CSV town 'Kullu' is approximate)
town_description: Chansari is a hillside village below the Bijli Mahadev hilltop, about 14 km from Kullu town, serving as the trek starting point for the temple. The area lies on the ridge between the Kullu and Parvati valleys, with panoramic Himalayan views. It is typical of the dispersed rural settlements of the valley, surrounded by deodar and pine forests and small farm terraces.

travel.road: Drive ~14 km from Kullu town to Chansari parking, then trek ~3 km uphill to the temple (easy-to-moderate)

visitor_information.best_time: March-September; may be inaccessible in winter snow (Dec-March) per one source (verify)
visitor_information.opening_hours: Daylight hours; plan to descend before dark (verify)
